data.hypothesis: For the selected 64x32 parent, replacing the padded 64x33 shared tile with a 64x32 XOR-swizzled layout may change shared-memory access behavior and reduce padding, but the indexing cost could offset any benefit. Prior measured variants show that the padded vector-ownership candidate (cef4bbb63e3e49cf, 3.142 us) was faster than the padded scalar 32x32 candidate (e8b5e81f11b14f29, 3.398 us), XOR-swizzled scalar 32x32 (5f05ca36bcd347ee, 3.253 us), and selected padded 64x32 parent (677cd6c7769f4f38, 3.703 us); this different 64x32 XOR layout tests rather than assumes the swizzle's value.

memory_lessons.applicability: This transpose's candidate choice should be measured against multiple distinct layouts; the best visible time does not establish that padding or XOR is intrinsically faster.
memory_lessons.claim: The visible valid, correct candidates span four distinct programs; the vectorized padded candidate measured 3.142 us, XOR scalar 3.253 us, padded scalar 3.398 us, and padded 64x32 parent 3.703 us. Layout and ownership variants have materially different observed outcomes.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the 64x32 XOR-swizzled program's controller-measured n=1024 repetitions and required-size correctness against these recorded candidates; retain no speed claim until measured.

data.notes: No commands were executed, so this candidate has no build, correctness, or timing result to report. The controller should build it, check exact correctness at n=32, 64, 256, and 1024, and report repeated complete-run n=1024 timings. Supplied prior evidence: baseline valid/correct, 16.919 us mean (samples 17.134, 16.749, 16.875 us); selected parent valid/correct, 3.703 us mean (3.705, 3.669, 3.735 us); cef4bbb63e3e49cf valid/correct, 3.142 us mean (3.181, 3.101, 3.144 us). Each reports eight correctness cases across n=32, 64, 256, 1024 and two seeds.
transformations: Changed the selected 64x32 transpose's shared tile from padded 64x33 storage to a 64x32 XOR-swizzled layout.
Applied the same row-dependent XOR mapping on load and transposed read so values retain their exact float bit patterns.
Preserved coalesced global load/store orientation, bounds checks, size_t indexing, the run entry point, and the existing allocation behavior.
